NEAR's fee burn plus Intents buybacks equal 11.8% of what it mints. Break-even is 8.5x away.

10.9% is NEAR sent by the NEAR Intents contract to the buyback account, where it is held, not burnt. 0.92% is gas fees burnt. A fee-burn dashboard sees only the second number and puts break-even 109x away.

Mint, burn and the buyback balance are read from NEAR mainnet, 2026-02-13 to 2026-11-12 (900 epochs, heights 185341924 to 224221936). Mint and burn are exact to the yoctoNEAR. Rebuild with python3 run.py: no keys, no network.

Payback was 3.1% in the first window with buyback data (2026-05-14), peaked at 16.5% (2026-09-19) and is 11.8% now.
11.8%of new issuance offset by burn plus buybacks

What closes the gap

Payback is burn plus buybacks over issuance. Three levers move it. Two of them are governance decisions, and one is in motion: HSP-029, passed by NEAR's House of Stake on 2026-11-02 and awaiting ratification, would lower maximum issuance to 1.6% a year.

Sender check: 2966 of the 2983 transfers since height 201009796 into the buyback account came from intents.near, carrying 73.9% of the NEAR (NearBlocks, with transaction hashes in data/inflows.csv).

The case against

  • Buybacks are held in a multisig account, not burnt. Supply does not fall and the NEAR can be spent.
  • Payback has fallen from its peak of 16.5% to 11.8%.
  • NEAR Intents is not growing: over a year, daily volume is 1.02x and gross fees 0.75x (DefiLlama).
  • One application supplies 92% of the payback.
  • Gas burn alone covers 0.92% of issuance, 109x from break-even.
